done_when: forge next says an item's worker is building only while its recorded worker process is alive; otherwise it says the worker stopped and names the next command; a test records a worker whose process has ended and sees the stopped message

findings.body: If a working item's lock exists but contains empty or partial JSON, `codex._json(lock)` returns `{}` and `codex._alive({})` returns `None`. This condition checks only for `False`, so `forge next` still says a worker is building even though the lock records no live worker. This can persist if a later work round is interrupted while writing its lock, since the earlier `working` status remains. Handle an invalid process record and test that output.
findings.title: Treat a lock without a valid process record as stopped

why: forge next says a worker is building items whose worker stopped long ago
